articles.title: ESG News Week In Review: 11 October – 31 October
articles.summary:
EU greenwashing penalties above 4% of turnover took effect on 16 October, Parliament pushed methane import compliance out to 2031, and France and Germany moved to soften the 2035 car […]
The post ESG News Week In Review: 11 October – 31 October appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
ESG News Week In Review: 11 October – 31 October
EU greenwashing penalties above 4% of turnover took effect on 16 October, Parliament pushed methane import compliance out to 2031, and France and Germany moved to soften the 2035 car target. The rules on what a company may say are tightening faster than the rules on what it must do.
The EU’s ban on unsubstantiated environmental claims took effect on 16 October, with member states able to impose penalties above 4% of annual turnover for serious breaches and blanket terms such as “eco” and “sustainable” no longer usable without evidence. The effects were visible almost immediately. Lufthansa renamed the Green Fare it launched in 2023 to Impact Fare. Coca-Cola, Nestle and Danone agreed to spell out that their “100%” recycling claims exclude the cap and the label, closing a BEUC complaint. ESMA published two thematic notes on impact and climate claims, then named materiality assessments among its 2026 enforcement priorities. The marketing layer of corporate sustainability is now supervised disclosure.
The underlying obligations moved the other way. Parliament approved a three-year postponement of the EU methane import rules, giving importers until 31 May 2031 to demonstrate equivalence, a longer delay than the one year expected weeks earlier. France and Germany closed on a deal to cut the 2035 car emissions target to 90% and drop the additional compensation requirements. The Commission’s proposed Climate Resilience Law hands member states a common warming trajectory reaching 3 degrees by 2100 and puts the adaptation bill at roughly 70 billion euro a year. Brussels is policing the claim harder than the conduct behind it.
Capital concentrated around electricity for computing. Blackstone closed Energy Transition Partners V at its $8.7 billion hard cap, more than half again the size of its predecessor. American Electric Power committed $4 billion to a 702 MW Bloom Energy fuel cell plant in Wyoming serving Google. Amazon funded feasibility work on a twelve-unit, 960 MW X-energy project in Indiana. Google and Voltus agreed to scale a virtual power plant tenfold to 1 GW across PJM, and 32 lenders backed AirTrunk with an A$4.25 billion green loan for a single Western Sydney campus. TPG closed Rise Climate II and its Global South Initiative at $10.4 billion combined.
The accounting underneath moved too. California fixed 10 November 2026 as the first Scope 1 and 2 reporting deadline under SB 253, and Thailand’s SEC told SET50 companies to report 2027 data on ISSB standards with assurance, while FTSE Russell found 84% of asset owners now factor in sustainability against Morgan Stanley’s finding that only 2% expect large allocation increases. The story to carry forward is the GHG Protocol’s Scope 2 proposal. Its Independent Standards Board has put an hourly-matched Method 1 beside the 2015 market-based rules, and a dated cut-off after which reporters must use Method 1 wherever qualifying data exists would reprice every annual renewable energy certificate and every power purchase agreement written on the old logic. The consolidated consultation slated for 2027 is where that date gets set.

articles.title: Masdar Breaks Ground on 200MW Chereh Floating Solar Plant
articles.summary:
Masdar, Citaglobal Berhad and TIZA Global Sdn Bhd have started building the 200-megawatt (MW) Chereh Dam Floating Solar PV Project in Pahang, Malaysia. The project reached financial close on 27 […]
The post Masdar Breaks Ground on 200MW Chereh Floating Solar Plant appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Masdar Breaks Ground on 200MW Chereh Floating Solar Plant
- Construction starts: Masdar, Citaglobal and TIZA Global broke ground on the 200MW Chereh Dam floating solar plant in Pahang.
- Financing closed: The project reached financial close on 27 October with about MYR 580 million from three international lenders.
- Masdar’s Malaysian debut: Chereh is Masdar’s first project in Malaysia and the first under its 10GW roadmap with MIDA.
Masdar, Citaglobal Berhad and TIZA Global Sdn Bhd have started building the 200-megawatt (MW) Chereh Dam Floating Solar PV Project in Pahang, Malaysia. The project reached financial close on 27 October, raising about 580 million Malaysian ringgit (MYR) from three international lenders. Chereh Solar Sdn Bhd, the partners’ project company, expects the plant to start operating in 2028.
The plant is expected to power the equivalent of 100,000 homes and create about 1,500 jobs during development and construction. It sits on an existing reservoir, and a Site Agreement with Pahang Water & Energy Resources supports its development. His Excellency Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, Chief Minister of Pahang, attended the groundbreaking with senior leaders from the partners. “Pahang is committed to supporting initiatives that advance sustainable development and create lasting value for our people. The Chereh Floating Solar Project reflects how our natural resources can be used responsibly to contribute to Malaysia’s renewable energy ambitions, while bringing opportunities for local communities and industry. I look forward to seeing the project deliver meaningful benefits for Pahang and the nation,” said His Royal Highness Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, the Sultan of Pahang.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
Masdar brings floating solar experience, including the 145MW Cirata project in Indonesia. Meanwhile, Citaglobal adds infrastructure and energy development capabilities, and TIZA Global adds local stakeholder engagement experience. “Malaysia is a strategically important market for Masdar, with rising electricity demand, strong renewable energy potential and growing investment in advanced industries and digital infrastructure. As our first project in the country, Chereh marks an important milestone in our long-term commitment to Malaysia and our expansion across Southeast Asia. By combining Masdar’s global floating solar expertise with strong local partnerships, we will support Malaysia’s energy ambitions while creating jobs and new economic opportunities in Pahang,” said Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, Chief Executive Officer of Masdar.
From Tender Win to Financial Close
In December 2025, Chereh Solar Sdn Bhd signed a 21-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with national utility Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB). The consortium won the project in Malaysia’s Large Scale Solar (LSS) Cycle 5+ tender, offering the lowest floating solar tariff. The partners did not disclose the total project cost, the lenders’ names or each partner’s equity stake. “The start of construction at Chereh is an important step in building Citaglobal’s renewable power generation portfolio. With long-term electricity sales contracted to TNB, the priority now is to deliver the project and bring it into operation. Citaglobal and TIZA Global will work closely with Masdar and the project team, drawing on our infrastructure and local development experience to support delivery in Pahang,” said Tan Sri Dato’ Sri (Dr.) Mohamad Norza Zakaria, Executive Chairman and President of Citaglobal Berhad and TIZA Global Sdn Bhd.
RELATED ARTICLE: Masdar, EPCG Advance 2GW Montenegro Energy Plan
Why It Matters
For Masdar, Chereh is the first project under the 10-gigawatt (GW) roadmap it agreed with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) in 2023. For Citaglobal, the project adds contracted generation to its New Energy platform, which spans solar, hydropower and Bio-CNG (compressed biogas). Masdar is also studying a major floating solar installation at the Murum reservoir in Sarawak. If Chereh starts operating in 2028, it could give the partners 21 years of TNB revenue and Masdar a reference case for Murum.

articles.title: Bank of America, Eurazeo Back $40 Million Nature Initiative
articles.summary:
The Sustainable Markets Initiative (SMI) and Bank of America have catalysed the Lighthouse Initiative, a dedicated Nature and biodiversity investment allocation. Eurazeo will manage it within its Future Industries Fund […]
The post Bank of America, Eurazeo Back $40 Million Nature Initiative appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Bank of America, Eurazeo Back $40 Million Nature Initiative
- Initial commitments: Launched on September 23, 2026 with $40 million in aggregate capital commitments.
- Minority stakes: It will back project development platforms and technology-enabled solutions in developed and emerging markets.
- Biodiversity targets: Each investment should support at least one Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework target.
The Sustainable Markets Initiative (SMI) and Bank of America have catalysed the Lighthouse Initiative, a dedicated Nature and biodiversity investment allocation. Eurazeo will manage it within its Future Industries Fund III. Bank of America and Eurazeo are the cornerstone investors, with $40 million in commitments at the September 23 launch.
The initiative aims to channel private capital into Nature business models that remain underfunded today. It is structured to welcome further investment from additional partners, and it aligns with Terra Carta, the SMI mandate launched by the former Prince of Wales in 2021. “The Lighthouse Initiative’s launch represents the global economic leadership and impact of the Sustainable Markets Initiative. Nature is a fundamental pillar of our mandate and is the true engine of our economy. The Lighthouse Initiative will mobilise much needed private capital into Nature and Nature-based solutions. It represents our unique ability to harness the power of the private sector to deliver results for Nature, people and planet,” said Jennifer Jordan-Saifi, President and Global Envoy of the Sustainable Markets Initiative.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
The initiative will make minority investments across developed and emerging markets. Each deal should support at least one framework target, such as Target 3, known as “30×30.” That target aims to conserve at least 30% of the world’s land, inland water, coastal and marine areas by 2030. The partners did not disclose a target size, a timeline for further closes or each cornerstone investor’s share.
Investment Priorities
Four priorities guide the strategy, starting with ecosystem protection and Nature regeneration, such as regenerative agriculture and forestry. The initiative will also support Nature-positive industries and supply chains, including bio-based materials and circular processes. In addition, it will back project platforms on infrastructure-like models that can attract institutional and public co-investors. Finally, it targets impact tracking tools such as eDNA (environmental DNA) monitoring and digital MRV (measurement, reporting and verification) platforms.
Eurazeo’s Future Industries team will manage the initiative. Investments will be tracked through Eurazeo’s impact framework, enhanced with biodiversity indicators such as a biodiversity footprint assessment. “Companies and investors are seeking opportunities to invest in Nature and biodiversity. Eurazeo has a demonstrated track record supporting hundreds of companies and the Lighthouse Initiative can help create even more opportunity,” said Brian Moynihan, Chair and CEO of Bank of America and Chair of the Sustainable Markets Initiative. “We are honoured that the Sustainable Markets Initiative and Bank of America have entrusted us with the management of this project. Nature is the foundation of the industries we invest in, yet biodiversity remains one of the most underfunded investment themes. With this initiative, we want to demonstrate that protecting and restoring Nature makes commercial sense, at scale. At Eurazeo, and within the Future Industries team, sustainability and impact are at the core of our business strategy model and we look forward to working to bring more investors behind the entrepreneurs building Nature-positive businesses,” said Matthieu Bonamy, Partner Future Industries at Eurazeo.
RELATED ARTICLE: Bank of America Issues $2 Billion ESG Bonds
Why It Matters
The mandate gives Eurazeo’s Future Industries team a dedicated Nature allocation inside Fund III. For Bank of America, the cornerstone stake adds direct exposure to Nature project platforms and technology-enabled solutions. Because the vehicle is open to new partners, it positions Eurazeo to raise co-investment from institutional and development finance investors. That depends on early deals proving the commercial case for protecting Nature.

articles.title: Green Climate Fund Commits $1.97 Billion to 21 Projects, Lifting Annual Approvals to a Record $3.2 Billion
articles.summary:
The Green Climate Fund (GCF), the world’s biggest multilateral climate investment fund, approved $1.97 billion for 21 projects at its latest board meeting. The approvals lift its funding for the […]
The post Green Climate Fund Commits $1.97 Billion to 21 Projects, Lifting Annual Approvals to a Record $3.2 Billion appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Green Climate Fund Commits $1.97 Billion to 21 Projects, Lifting Annual Approvals to a Record $3.2 Billion
- Record board approvals: The Green Climate Fund approved $1.97 billion for 21 projects, including $682 million for six private-sector initiatives.
- Higher leverage goal: Executive Director Mafalda Duarte wants the fund to mobilise more than $10 for every $1 it invests.
- Broader funding base: A first-ever policy allows contributions from non-sovereign and alternative sources ahead of the fund’s third replenishment round.
The Green Climate Fund (GCF), the world’s biggest multilateral climate investment fund, approved $1.97 billion for 21 projects at its latest board meeting. The approvals lift its funding for the year to a record $3.2 billion, Mafalda Duarte, the fund’s executive director, told Reuters. They include $682 million for six private-sector initiatives.
The fund has historically mobilised $3 of additional resources for every $1 it invests. For its private-sector projects, that ratio has been $4.5. It rose to $9 last year, but Duarte said there was further to go. “We should be talking about multipliers that are higher than 10 for each dollar of GCF resources,” Duarte said, adding that she was being “very conservative”.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
The approvals come ahead of the COP31 climate talks in Turkey in early November. Richer countries are reluctant to commit more money as they face other financial and political pressures. Meanwhile, the fund is preparing for its third replenishment round, when contributors pledge new money. Duarte said a first-ever policy allowing contributions from non-sovereign and alternative sources could broaden its funding base beyond national governments.
To help move more money, Duarte said the fund is developing co-investment platforms. Through them, sovereign and non-sovereign investors could team up in particular sectors, projects and markets. Looking ahead to COP31, she said the fund had demand for more than $11 billion in funding. Duarte said she was hoping to see a “strong signal of political support and commitment towards a very strong replenishment”.
Portfolio Track Record
The latest approvals take the fund’s total investments to $22.3 billion across 379 projects. Including co-financing, meaning money committed by other investors alongside the GCF, the portfolio reaches $86.4 billion. The fund did not name the 21 projects or their host countries, or say what size of replenishment it is seeking.
RELATED ARTICLE: Green Climate Fund Approves Record $1.225B for Climate Projects
Why It Matters
The record $3.2 billion in annual approvals gives the GCF a larger pipeline to present to contributors before its third replenishment. Paired with the new non-sovereign contribution policy, that record could open a path to replenishment capital from investors beyond national governments. The outcome depends on whether the planned co-investment platforms attract those backers as donor governments hold back.

articles.summary:
Germany-based sustainability software company osapiens has appointed Stephan de Barse to the newly created position of President. He will lead all of the company’s go-to-market activities, including sales, marketing, business […]
The post Osapiens Appoints Stephan de Barse as President to Lead All Go-to-Market Teams appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Osapiens Appoints Stephan de Barse as President to Lead All Go-to-Market Teams
- New President role: Stephan de Barse takes a newly created President position at osapiens.
- Single go-to-market unit: The role covers sales, marketing, business development, solution engineering and partnerships.
- Series C backing: The company announced a $100 million Series C round earlier this year.
Germany-based sustainability software company osapiens has appointed Stephan de Barse to the newly created position of President. He will lead all of the company’s go-to-market activities, including sales, marketing, business development, solution engineering and partnerships.
According to osapiens, the new position brings these go-to-market activities together under one roof. The company said the structure reflects the pace of the market, as companies face growing regulatory complexity. At the same time, they must manage supplier risk and resilience across climate, geopolitical risk, sanctions and financial exposure. “Compliance is at an inflection point: regulation keeps growing, and companies need to manage risk and increase resilience across their supply chains at the same time. By bringing sales, marketing, business development, solution engineering and partnerships together, we give customers one strategy and one experience from day one through long-term value,” said de Barse.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
Founded in 2018, osapiens provides cloud-based software to automate compliance tasks, streamline operations and track sustainability metrics in real time. The software also helps clients comply with national and international sustainability regulations. Earlier this year, it announced a $100 million Series C round led by BlackRock and Temasek’s decarbonization-focused fund, Decarbonization Partners. It also recently announced the acquisition of Nasdaq Metrio, Nasdaq’s sustainability reporting and carbon accounting software platform.
From Revenue Chief to President
De Barse joined osapiens as Chief Revenue Officer earlier this year from SAP. At SAP, he served as President of the Business Suite Organization. Before that, he was Chief Revenue Officer at enterprise planning software provider o9 Solutions. Osapiens did not disclose when the appointment takes effect or who will take over the Chief Revenue Officer role.
RELATED ARTICLE: ERM, osapiens Partner to Turn ESG Compliance Data Into Business Action
Why It Matters
For osapiens, the change puts one executive in charge of every team that sells its compliance software. That remit now also covers the Nasdaq Metrio reporting and carbon accounting platform. The structure positions osapiens to cross-sell Metrio’s carbon accounting tools to its existing compliance clients through one go-to-market team, provided the platforms are integrated.

articles.title: Schneider Electric to Recruit 50 Engineers Across Five Hubs for AI-Focused Energy Program
articles.summary:
Schneider Electric has launched Energy Tech Accelerator, a 12-month global early-career program for engineers. The company will recruit an inaugural cohort of 50 participants across five global hubs. Participants will […]
The post Schneider Electric to Recruit 50 Engineers Across Five Hubs for AI-Focused Energy Program appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Schneider Electric to Recruit 50 Engineers Across Five Hubs for AI-Focused Energy Program
- Inaugural cohort: Schneider Electric will recruit 50 early-career participants for its new Energy Tech Accelerator program.
- Two rotations: Each participant will complete two six-month rotations over 12 months, with learning, mentoring and customer exposure.
- Five global hubs: The cohort will be based in Boston, Paris and Grenoble, Dubai, Bangalore, and Shanghai.
Schneider Electric has launched Energy Tech Accelerator, a 12-month global early-career program for engineers. The company will recruit an inaugural cohort of 50 participants across five global hubs. Participants will work at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), engineering and sustainable energy.
Each participant will complete two six-month rotations based in Boston, Paris and Grenoble, Dubai, Bangalore, or Shanghai. They will tackle business and customer challenges while receiving dedicated learning, mentoring and customer exposure. The program also aims to build a connected global community among participants. “At Schneider, our goal is to Advance Energy Tech to the next level to deliver greater business outcomes for our customers. By leveraging Data & AI, we connect the physical and digital worlds to deliver Energy & Industrial Intelligence to our Customers,” said Olivier Blum, chief executive officer of Schneider Electric. “Turning that intelligence into solutions that help our customers operate more efficiently and sustainably requires people who can combine deep knowledge of energy and industrial processes with AI. That is why we are launching Energy Tech Accelerator: to attract and develop people who understand AI, are passionate about the energy transition and want to make a tangible contribution to a more sustainable future.”
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
Energy Tech Accelerator is part of Schneider Electric’s investment in workforce capabilities as energy systems become more digital and connected. The company said the program gives emerging talent responsibility and practical experience from the start. “Advancing energy technology is ultimately about people,” said Charise Le, chief human resources officer of Schneider Electric. “Early-career talent should not have to wait years to make a meaningful contribution. Through Energy Tech Accelerator, participants will learn across the business, take on real challenges and build the capabilities and confidence to help shape a more sustainable energy future.”
Schneider Electric is targeting curious, analytical and globally minded early-career engineers. It wants candidates who are excited by AI, digital technology and sustainable transformation. Applications open Nov. 2, and candidates can apply through the Energy Tech Accelerator page on Schneider Electric’s careers site. However, the company did not disclose the program’s budget, the cohort’s start date or an application deadline.
RELATED ARTICLE: Schneider Electric Backs New Climate Impact Framework
Why It Matters
Energy Tech Accelerator gives Schneider Electric a dedicated pipeline of 50 engineers trained in both AI and energy processes. Blum tied that skill mix directly to delivering Energy & Industrial Intelligence, built on data and AI, to customers. Because rotations focus on customer challenges, participants also build client-facing experience within their first year. If the first cohort completes both rotations, the company could staff more AI-based efficiency projects for customers from within its own ranks.

articles.title: Iberdrola, NBIM Add 274 MW Portuguese Wind Farm to Iberian Co-Investment Platform
articles.summary:
Iberdrola and Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM) have added the 274-megawatt (MW) Tâmega wind project to their Iberian co-investment platform. The wind farm, located in northern Portugal, is already in […]
The post Iberdrola, NBIM Add 274 MW Portuguese Wind Farm to Iberian Co-Investment Platform appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Iberdrola, NBIM Add 274 MW Portuguese Wind Farm to Iberian Co-Investment Platform
- Tâmega wind added: The 274 MW Tâmega wind project in northern Portugal, already in commercial operation, joins the co-investment platform.
- Portfolio passes 1,800 MW: The platform’s total capacity now exceeds 1,800 MW after the latest closing.
- 2,300 MW targeted: The partners expect to reach 2,300 MW by next year, backed by more than €2 billion of investment.
Iberdrola and Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM) have added the 274-megawatt (MW) Tâmega wind project to their Iberian co-investment platform. The wind farm, located in northern Portugal, is already in commercial operation. As a result, the alliance’s renewable portfolio now exceeds 1,800 MW of total capacity.
The partners expect the platform to keep adding renewable capacity and reach 2,300 MW by next year. The alliance is backed by more than €2 billion of investment. It also forms part of a long-term strategic alliance to accelerate electrification. However, the companies did not disclose the Tâmega deal value, the ownership split or the projects behind the remaining capacity.
According to the companies, Iberdrola is Europe’s largest utility and one of the two largest worldwide by market capitalisation. NBIM, one of the world’s largest sovereign wealth funds, manages assets of around €2.1 trillion. It holds stakes in more than 9,000 companies, averaging 1.5% of all listed companies globally and 2.5% across Europe. The companies also say the partnership could extend into renewable projects in additional markets.
What’s New
Tâmega follows the addition of 646 MW of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity to the joint venture earlier this year. That capacity comes from the Caparacena and Ciudad Rodrigo plants in Spain, in operation since the end of last year. The alliance began as NBIM’s first direct investment in renewable assets in Spain, so Tâmega adds operating wind capacity in Portugal. Meanwhile, NBIM has held around 2.3% of Iberdrola for more than seven years.
Why It Matters
For Iberdrola, the closing moves another operating asset into a joint venture with one of its largest shareholders. For NBIM, Tâmega extends its direct renewable holdings from Spanish solar into Portuguese wind. If the platform reaches its 2,300 MW goal on schedule, it could give Iberdrola an established co-investor for renewables beyond Spain and Portugal.

articles.title: Google Funds $160 Million Water Plant in Negeri Sembilan
articles.summary:
Google has committed $160 million to build shared water infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. The funds will pay for an off-river storage reservoir and a water treatment plant. When complete, […]
The post Google Funds $160 Million Water Plant in Negeri Sembilan appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Google Funds $160 Million Water Plant in Negeri Sembilan
- $160 million commitment: Google will fund an off-river storage reservoir and water treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia.
- Shared daily supply: The plant will supply 65 million liters of drinking water a day for public use and Google’s planned campus.
- State ownership: Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Incorporated, a state statutory body, will own the facilities after completion.
Google has committed $160 million to build shared water infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. The funds will pay for an off-river storage reservoir and a water treatment plant. When complete, the plant will supply 65 million liters (17.17 million gallons) of drinking water a day. That supply will serve public use as well as Google’s planned data center campus in Port Dickson.
Google partnered with the Negeri Sembilan state government and water utility Syarikat Air Negeri Sembilan Sdn Bhd on the project. It appointed Gamuda Berhad, a Malaysia-based engineering and construction company, to build the reservoir and treatment plant. Once construction ends, Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Incorporated, a state statutory body that holds assets, will own the facilities. Google did not disclose a completion date or how much of the daily supply its campus will use.
Separately, Google has committed to pay for 100 percent of the power its Port Dickson campus requires. It will also cover the direct infrastructure costs of connecting the campus to the grid. Meanwhile, Google is expanding its work with SOLS Foundation to start two clean energy training initiatives for young people. “Google’s decision to fund shared water infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan reflects our global ambition to replenish 120 percent of the freshwater volume we consume, even as our water risk assessment showed that local water sources were not at high risk of scarcity or depletion. This underscores our responsibility to grow our presence sustainably—pairing advanced digital infrastructure development with water replenishment projects, power infrastructure enhancements, and programs designed to upskill local talent for new career opportunities,” said Drew Byrnes, director and head of global infrastructure and energy, Asia Pacific, at Google.
Google’s Malaysia Build-Out
Google earlier bought 389 acres in Port Dickson, about 90km (55.9 miles) south of Kuala Lumpur, for the campus. Reports put its capacity at 500MW to 1GW, with Gamuda Engineering leading engineering and infrastructure works. In October 2024, Google broke ground at Selangor’s Elmina Business Park, where a 100MW first phase is expected. Both projects are part of the $2 billion Google committed to invest in Malaysia in 2024.
RELATED ARTICLE: Google Backs Texas Electric Freight Route
Why It Matters
For Google, the plant gives its Port Dickson campus a dedicated water source while adding drinking water for public use. For Gamuda, it adds a water treatment contract alongside its reported engineering role on the data center itself. Once complete, the plant positions Google to bring the campus online and turn part of its Malaysia investment into operating data center capacity.
